To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the most effective TLIR methods are those that use bilingual corpora to learn the translingual context of words, (ii) statistical methods that use bilingual corporas to learn the trans-lingual associations of words perform as well as the best monolingual methods, and (iii) query translation based on a machine-readable dictionary is less effective than statistical methods.
1) query translation is not a good approach to TLIR, 2) statistical-IR approaches are promising and 3) bilingual corpora are a valuable asset in TLIR research.

(i) query translation methods are outperformed by corpus-based approaches; (ii) the translingual version of the Generalized vector space model performs as well as its monolingual counterpart; (iii) LSI performs as well as other corpus-based approaches, and (iv) pseudo relevance feedback and example-based term translation are effective methods for translingual IR

the development of new methods for TLIR and with the comparative assessment of these and previous methods in a realistic TLIR setting.
the development of new TLIR methods, and with their evaluation in a realistic TLIR setting, which is a step toward the practical use of TLIR in real applications.

all the methods tested are promising and that the most promising methods are those that make use of bilingual corpora.
the best methods for translingual information retrieval in this setting use statistical methods based on bilingual corpora.

the best results are achieved by the statistical-IR approaches that establish translingual associations, and that the best results among these are achieved with the translingual versions of GVSM and LSI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective TLIR methods are those that use bilingual corpora, whether to establish translation equivalences, to build statistical-IR models or to use PRF.
statistical methods that learn from bilingual corpora outperform dictionary-based approaches, and that statistical methods that use translingual associations outperform query translation methods.
the best TLIR methods are based on statistical analysis of bilingual corpora, and that these methods can perform very well in realistic settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLIR is feasible, and that it is possible to achieve good performance using statistical IR methods that are based on bilingual corpora.
the performance of TLIR methods is comparable to that of monolingual methods, which means that there is no inherent performance penalty for using TLIR.
